name: Residences at Dry Cedar Creek
headline: Residences at Dry Cedar Creek is a 60-home mixed-income family rental complex (54 income-restricted, 6 market-rate) beside the Montrose Recreation Center, developed by RealAmerica Development with a 2022 Round One federal 9% credit award; it opened in October 2024.
why_it_matters: It is a built, fully leased Western Slope 9% deal whose ownership, city and housing-authority support and lease-up record (221-household waitlist) RealAmerica is now reusing for its neighbouring Cedar Creek Commons and Black Canyon Flats deals.

status.label: Built and occupied (opened October 2024)
status.detail: KREX reported the ribbon cutting on Tuesday 2024-10-08 (date inferred from the 2024-10-09 story) with 87% of homes leased; RealAmerica's 2026 CHFA application says it opened in October 2024, stabilized by December 2024 and is fully occupied with a 221-household waitlist. No placed-in-service or 8609 record was found online.

next_step: Watch Montrose County Assessor records for the housing-authority tax exemption and CHFA compliance listings for a placed-in-service date.

key_numbers.meaning: Six at 30% AMI, 21 at 50%, 27 at 60%, plus six market-rate homes.
About $13.5M over 10 years; no state credit is shown on the award report.
Named in the application and again in 2023 press coverage of the groundbreaking.
From the Montrose County Housing Authority, which also committed property and sales tax exemptions while the homes stay affordable.

facts.value: Two three-story wood-frame walk-up buildings plus a stand-alone community building; NGBS Silver target
Vacant infill site directly east of the Montrose Recreation Center; all buildings north of Dry Cedar Creek, leaving over four acres of open space to the south
R-2, to be rezoned to R-3A; Planning Commission voted 7-0 for the rezone on 2022-01-26, with council hearings to follow
RealAmerica Construction (in-house); factory-built and prefabricated components planned

money.note: Application requested $1,350,000; the narrative puts tax credit equity at $12,418,858.
Letter of interest at application; the 2023 press report gives about $1,890,000.

Building permit fees, city construction use tax and plan check fee; the city also signalled possible waivers of $311,808 in tap and unit charges. The 2023 press report puts total city support at about $935,000.
City project built to serve the complex; completed May 2024.

background.text: After a CHFA concept meeting on 2022-01-06, RealAmerica added seven affordable homes (four at 50% AMI, three at 60%) to reach 54 affordable and 6 market-rate homes.
The award report's asterisk is on its Market Units column; the footnote says housing tax credit proceeds will not be used to support the development of market-rate units.
The site was under contract at application, with closing scheduled on or before 2022-10-31. Seller and price are not public in the sources checked.

The Montrose County Housing Authority committed six project-based vouchers and property and sales tax exemptions for as long as the homes stay affordable (implies a housing-authority ownership role; structure not public).

The application cited zero vacancies across 554 low-income rental units in the market area, waiting lists at all four existing tax-credit properties, and the hospital's 100+ unfilled jobs blamed on housing.

The Montrose Press reported a groundbreaking ceremony in the week of 2023-10-12 with a mid-2024 completion target; it gave 30% AMI one-bedroom rents near $415 and 60% AMI three-bedroom rents over $1,200.
KREX reported a ribbon cutting in October 2024, with 12 one-bedroom, 36 two-bedroom and 12 three-bedroom homes and 87% leased; the developer said the project took about three years.
RealAmerica's 2026 Round One application for the adjacent Cedar Creek Commons says Dry Cedar Creek stabilized by December 2024 and holds a 221-household waitlist.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award report and the application give the address as 65919 Ogden Road, while the developer's property page gives 1906 Ogden Road.
The Montrose Press groundbreaking story describes 48 units with 42 at or below 60% AMI, while CHFA's award report, award description and the 2024 KREX opening story give 60 units (54 restricted).
The application counts $235,645 of city fee waivers (with up to $311,808 more possible), while the 2023 press report puts city support at about $935,000.
